append.text: **Ps 95:6 the noun *Conféssio, et pulchritúdo* → *Confissão e beleza*** (no articles, as the Latin): *ação de graças* does not fit (an attribute beside beauty), *louvor* is laudábilis's two verses earlier (95:4). The Latinist passed it twice; the ambiguity reader heard the confession of sins first — one of the two senses the Latin holds. **For Gustavo's ear**; 103:1 *Confessiónem et decórem* should decide with it. Options *Ação de graças*, *Louvor*.
**Ps 95:7 → *Trazei ao Senhor* ×3**, copying 28:1–2; passed the Latinist twice, no reader remarked.

append.row: | *Afférte Dómino … glóriam et honórem … afférte Dómino glóriam nómini ejus* (28:1–2; 95:7 *Afférte Dómino, pátriæ géntium, afférte Dómino glóriam et honórem: * afférte Dómino glóriam nómini ejus*) |
append.text: **Ps 95:7 copied: *Trazei ao Senhor, ó famílias das nações, trazei ao Senhor glória e honra: * trazei ao Senhor glória ao seu nome*** (pátriæ = famíliæ of 21:28b, one Greek πατριαί).

append.row: | *adoráte Dóminum in átrio sancto ejus* (28:2 = 95:8, word for word, grep) |
append.text: **Ps 95:8b copied.**
Ps 95:8 *in átria ejus … in átrio sancto ejus* → *nos seus átrios … no seu átrio santo*; unknown to the ambiguity reader again; kept.

**Ps 95:8 *Tóllite hóstias* → *Tomai vítimas*** (MS1932; the Latinist, minor on v1). v1 *Erguei vítimas* (= 23:7 *Attóllite → Erguei*, one Greek ἄρατε) was heard by the ambiguity reader as 'help the victims of harm'; so *tomar* now serves tóllere here and súmere at 80:3 (λάβετε), against D15's test, for a right first hearing. The stylist asked the article (*as vítimas*), option. v2 gate clean.
**Ps 95:12 *ómnia ligna silvárum* → *todas as árvores das selvas*** — the row, as it foresaw; no reader remarked on *árvores*.

**Ps 95:12 *ligna silvárum* → *árvores das selvas*** (MS1932, word for word) — D44 held; **the third psalm with the objection**: the v1 stylist asked *florestas*, the ambiguity reader heard 'jungles' first. For the coordinator; *florestas*, *matas* options in Ps 95's decision `silva`.

**Ps 95:10 *Étenim corréxit orbem terræ, qui non commovébitur* → *Pois ele endireitou o mundo, que não será abalado*** (92:1b's build with the Latin's other verb); **95:13 *Judicábit orbem terræ in æquitáte* → *Julgará o mundo com equidade*** (= 9:8b).

**Ps 95:10 *corréxit* → *endireitou*, not *corrigiu*** — the v1 stylist heard *corrigiu o mundo* as grading homework and the ambiguity reader as 'corrected / punished'; *endireitar* is L&S's first sense ('to make straight') and the Greek's (κατώρθωσεν), and keeps the moral sense in Portuguese. The v2 Latinist passed it. Cost: *endireitai* is the open imperative of dirígere (D22) — another form, and the two do not meet here. *corrigiu* option. So *corrígere* now has *corrigir* (17:36b) and *endireitar* (95:10).

**Ps 95:9, 95:11 jussive *Commoveátur* → *Abale-se*** (pronominal: verb first as the Latin, no gendered participle); 95:10 *qui non commovébitur* → *que não será abalado*; the verb three times in three verses, as the Latin. The ambiguity reader heard 'tremble, be shaken' and, of the sea, 'be stirred'. *Seja abalada / abalado* option.
Ps 95:11 *commoveátur mare, et plenitúdo ejus* → *abale-se o mar, e a sua plenitude* — the formula; the ambiguity reader found it vague but heard 'everything that fills it' first.

**Ps 95:2 *annuntiáte de die in diem salutáre ejus* → *anunciai de dia em dia a sua salvação*** — both places now agree; the ambiguity reader heard 'every day' first ('little by little' second). Ready to settle.

**Ps 95:2 *benedícite nómini ejus* (dative) → *bendizei o seu nome*** — the v1 stylist: *bendizer a* sounds dated and the second *ao* blurs into *ao Senhor* just before. Taken as grammar (D2), as 28:11 already made a dative direct. The row's 'dative → *ao*' may want revisiting: with a noun object the direct object is how Brazil says it. *bendizei ao seu nome* option.

Ps 95:4 *terríbilis est super omnes deos* → *é terrível acima de todos os deuses* (*super* → *acima de*: rank; *sobre* option, *mais que* MS1932 option); the ambiguity reader heard 'horrible' first again, then 'fearsome' from context. 94:3 and 96:9 (*super omnes deos*) should agree on the preposition.

append.row: | *Magnus Dóminus, et laudábilis nimis* (47:2; 95:4 *Quóniam magnus Dóminus et laudábilis nimis*, 144:3 — grep; the Matins antiphon, the Pent08-0 Gradual (*valde*), the Holy Thursday Mandatum) |
append.text: **Ps 95:4 → *Porque grande é o Senhor, e muito digno de louvor*** — copied; the v1 stylist heard *Senhor … louvor* as a jingle at the mediant and asked *o Senhor é grande*: refused for the formula (option in Ps 95 decision `magnus`); if taken, 47:2 and 144:3 follow.
**Ps 95:6 *in conspéctu ejus* with a copula → *estão na sua presença*** (21:28b, 49:3b): *estão à vista dele* would be heard as 'are visible to him'. *à vista dele*, *diante dele* options.

**The verb, Ps 95:11 *gaudébunt campi* → *os campos se regozijarão*** — a third verb of joy beside *læténtur → alegrem-se* and *exsúltet → exulte* in one verse (χαρήσεται against εὐφραινέσθωσαν / ἀγαλλιάσθω, D15's test); *regozijar-se* was free. MS1932 *alegrar-se-ão* option. No reader remarked.

**Ps 95:6 *sanctimónia et magnificéntia* → *santidade e magnificência*** — the row; unknown to the ambiguity reader (the third blind reader); passed the Latinist twice. *sanctimónia* (ἁγιωσύνη) → *santidade*, the Greek of 29:5 *sanctitátis*.
**Ps 95:6 *Conféssio, et pulchritúdo* → *Confissão e beleza*** — *beleza* for pulchritúdo as this row reserved; 103:1 *Confessiónem, et decórem* will be *esplendor*.
Note from Ps 95:10: *endireitar* now also renders *corréxit* (*endireitou o mundo*, readers' fault with *corrigiu*); weigh it when this row is ruled.

append.row: | *Dóminus regnávit, decórem indútus est: * indútus est Dóminus fortitúdinem, et præcínxit se* (92:1a; *Dóminus regnávit* opens 96:1 and 98:1; the antiphon *Dóminus regnávit, decórem índuit*, Psalmi major and missa Nat1-0 — grep) |
append.text: **Ps 95:9 *dícite in géntibus quia Dóminus regnávit* → *dizei entre as nações que o Senhor reinou*** — the formula inside reported speech (the Latin's *quia*; the Greek is direct, option). The ambiguity reader heard *reinou* as past and puzzling — the tense's known cost.

terms: | sanctificátio (ἁγίασμα, a holy place) | santificação (*santidade e magnificência na sua santificação*) | open | Ps 95:6, after 77:54 *o monte da sua santificação* (the same Greek). The Latin's word kept where DRB and MS1932 say sanctuary; the ambiguity reader heard 'his act of making holy', sense unclear, and did not know the word — the cost. *no seu santuário* option. Other places (grep): 13:15 (a canticle file), 36:15 and 131:8 (*arca sanctificatiónis tuæ*), 96:12 *memóriæ sanctificatiónis ejus*. |

| pátria (πατριά, a clan) | família (*ó famílias das nações*) | open | Ps 95:7 *pátriæ géntium* = 21:28b *famíliæ géntium* (one Greek, αἱ πατριαὶ τῶν ἐθνῶν; D15's test). MS1932. *linhagens* (DRB 'kindreds') option. No reader remarked. |

| dæmónium | demônio (*todos os deuses das nações são demônios*) | open | Ps 95:5 (δαιμόνια; the Hebrew's 'idols' refused, rule 1); = 90:6 *o demônio do meio-dia*. The ambiguity reader heard devils. 105:37 *fílias suas dæmóniis* should follow (grep; also canticle 32:25). |

| tóllere (hóstias) | tomar (*Tomai vítimas*) | open | Ps 95:8 (ἄρατε). The Greek is 23:7's *Attóllite → Erguei*, but *Erguei vítimas* was heard as helping victims; the Latinist asked *Tomai* (MS1932). Shares *tomar* with súmere (80:3). |

| gaudére | regozijar-se (*os campos se regozijarão*) | open | Ps 95:11, beside lætári → alegrar-se and exsultáre → exultar in the same verse (χαίρω, a third Greek verb). Free till now (the gáudium row lists *regozijo* as unused). |
